proposal.scope_review: Learner drives an ordinary passenger car. This sign affects that car driver directly; no specialist vehicle operation is taught.
proposal.scenario: Ordinary two-way countryside road emerging from a broad gentle bend into a clear straight section, no motorway, no tunnel, no junction. On right verge a SQUARE BLUE sign with WHITE number "70" crossed by a thick RED DIAGONAL rising from bottom-left to top-right, precisely C4b. Blue square must remain square, not a red-bordered white circular speed limit. No other signs or numerical overlays.
proposal.novelty_review: Complements existing C4a advisory-speed recognition by identifying its end; distinguishes end of advice from end of a mandatory maximum, with no new speed entitlement.

Natural daylight, realistic scale and perspective, neutral exposure, no cinematic grading. fr.question_text: Que signifie ce panneau carré bleu barré ?
fr.answer_a: La fin de la vitesse conseillée à 70 km/h.
fr.answer_b: Une vitesse minimale obligatoire de 70 km/h.
fr.explanation: Le panneau C4b met fin à la vitesse conseillée indiquée, ici 70 km/h. Il ne supprime pas les limitations de vitesse applicables et ne m’ordonne pas d’accélérer : je continue à adapter mon allure aux conditions de circulation.

en.question_text: What does this crossed-out blue square sign mean?
en.answer_a: The end of the advised speed of 70 km/h.
en.answer_b: A mandatory minimum speed of 70 km/h.
en.explanation: Sign C4b ends the indicated advised speed, here 70 km/h. It does not cancel applicable speed limits or require acceleration: I continue to adapt my speed to traffic and road conditions.

review_note: Actual image reviewed: square blue 70 with red ascending cancellation bar; not circular B33 or B43. Gentle rural curve does not justify automatic acceleration, which the explanation explicitly rejects. End of advisory speed is the only correct answer A in both languages.
